## 🌍 World politics & geopolitics

- <a id="st-fb7d688d5a1f" class="st-a"></a>**Final results of Israel's election of Tuesday 27 October, published overnight into Friday 30 October, confirm a hung Knesset: Benjamin Netanyahu's outgoing coalition has 53 of 120 seats and the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot has 48.** A government needs 61 seats. Netanyahu's Likud remains the largest party with 27 seats. The two Arab-led lists, Ra'am and the United List, won 19 seats between them, an unprecedented result, and turnout was close to 78%. Likud has alleged that Qatar paid to buy votes for the Arab parties. Qatar and the Arab parties reject the claim. Police said they had no evidence for it, and the Central Elections Committee called some of the circulating claims "entirely unfounded", adding that the separate Shin Bet investigation will not affect the results. Left-wing Democrats leader Yair Golan has met Eisenkot, Yair Lapid and Ra'am's Mansour Abbas and called for talks with the Arab-led parties. The results go to President Isaac Herzog on Wednesday 4 November, after which he will choose who gets the first chance to form a government. [ongoing since 2026-10-27] [RFI, 30 Oct 2026](https://www.rfi.fr/fr/moyen-orient/20261030-l%C3%A9gislatives-en-isra%C3%ABl-le-camp-de-benyamin-netanyahu-en-t%C3%AAte-mais-sans-majorit%C3%A9) · [DW, 30 Oct 2026](https://www.dw.com/en/israeli-election-netanyahu-main-rival-fall-short-of-majority-after-all-votes-counted/live-79713839)
  Why it matters: neither bloc can govern without either a unity deal or support from the Arab-led parties, and the right-wing parties in Eisenkot's own bloc may resist relying on the latter. Which government emerges will largely decide whether Israel's policy in Gaza continues on its current course.
